postTitle: Life Events and Your Finances: How to Plan Ahead
topic: Plan what you can see coming, buffer what you cannot

assumptions.notes: Emergency fund: a common guideline of three to six months of expenses (from the emergency fund post). No other figures. Illustrative.

buffers: An emergency fund, often 3 to 6 months of costs
A plan with slack in it
columnStory.disclosure: Illustrative. 3 to 6 months is a common guideline, not a rule.

hookVariants.narration: Most money shocks are not shocks. You knew they were coming.
There are two kinds of life event, and they need opposite plans.
One question sorts every big money event: can you name roughly when it happens?

beats.narration: Petra can see some of hers years ahead. A child. A bigger home. A career break. A move abroad.
beats.subtext: A child, a home, a break, a move

beats.narration: Those get a plan. Put each one in your projection, with a rough date and a number, and test the bad case.
beats.subtext: A date, a number, the bad case

beats.narration: Others nobody can see coming. An illness. A redundancy. A family emergency. A market shock.
Those cannot be planned one by one. They get a buffer instead.
beats.subtext: Not a plan for each one

beats.narration: Three buffers do most of the work. An emergency fund, often three to six months of costs. The right insurance. And a plan with some slack in it.
The expensive mistake is mixing them up. Treating a planned baby as a surprise, or trying to predict every disaster.
beats.subtext: A planned baby is not a surprise

beats.narration: So sort every event with one question. Can you name roughly when it happens? Then plan it. If not, buffer it.

cta.narration: Save this, and sort your next five years tonight.

caption.instagram:
Most money shocks are not shocks. You knew they were coming.

Some life events you can see years ahead: a child, a home, a career break, a move abroad. Those get a plan: a rough date, a number, and the bad case tested. Others nobody sees coming: an illness, a redundancy, a family emergency, a market shock. Those get a buffer: an emergency fund (a common guideline is three to six months of costs), the right insurance, and a plan with some slack.

The sorting question: can you name roughly when it happens? Then plan it. If not, buffer it.
